statement: Whenever max_points returns a result ans, len(ans) = k and for every i with 0 <= i < k, ans[i] is equal to the number of pairs (r,c) such that 0 <= r < m, 0 <= c < n, and there exists a finite sequence of cells (r_0,c_0), ..., (r_t,c_t) with t >= 0, (r_0,c_0) = (0,0), (r_t,c_t) = (r,c), each consecutive pair differing by exactly 1 in one coordinate and 0 in the other, and grid[r_s][c_s] < queries[i] for every s with 0 <= s <= t.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). We assume m >= 1; n >= 1; every row grid[r] with 0 <= r < m has length exactly n; m*n <= 100000; for every r,c with 0 <= r < m and 0 <= c < n, 1 <= grid[r][c] <= 1000000; and k = len(queries) satisfies 1 <= k <= 10000. The entries of queries may be arbitrary 64-bit integers. All indices are 0-based.

statement: Under the preconditions, max_points returns a result ans; it does not panic, fail an overflow check, or access grid, a row of grid, or queries out of bounds.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). We assume m >= 1; n >= 1; every row grid[r] with 0 <= r < m has length exactly n; m*n <= 100000; for every r,c with 0 <= r < m and 0 <= c < n, 1 <= grid[r][c] <= 1000000; and k = len(queries) satisfies 1 <= k <= 10000. The entries of queries may be arbitrary 64-bit integers. All indices are 0-based.

statement: Whenever max_points returns a result ans, len(ans) = len(queries) = k.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). We assume m >= 1; n >= 1; every row grid[r] with 0 <= r < m has length exactly n; m*n <= 100000; for every r,c with 0 <= r < m and 0 <= c < n, 1 <= grid[r][c] <= 1000000; and k = len(queries) satisfies 1 <= k <= 10000. The entries of queries may be arbitrary 64-bit integers. All indices are 0-based.

statement: Whenever max_points returns a result ans, for every i with 0 <= i < k, 0 <= ans[i] <= m*n.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). statement: Whenever max_points returns a result ans, for every i with 0 <= i < k, ans[i] <= N_i, where N_i is the number of pairs (r,c) with 0 <= r < m, 0 <= c < n, and grid[r][c] < queries[i].
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). We assume m >= 1; n >= 1; every row grid[r] with 0 <= r < m has length exactly n; m*n <= 100000; for every r,c with 0 <= r < m and 0 <= c < n, 1 <= grid[r][c] <= 1000000; and k = len(queries) satisfies 1 <= k <= 10000. The entries of queries may be arbitrary 64-bit integers. All indices are 0-based.

statement: Whenever max_points returns a result ans, for every i with 0 <= i < k, ans[i] = 0 if and only if queries[i] <= grid[0][0].
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). We assume m >= 1; n >= 1; every row grid[r] with 0 <= r < m has length exactly n; m*n <= 100000; for every r,c with 0 <= r < m and 0 <= c < n, 1 <= grid[r][c] <= 1000000; and k = len(queries) satisfies 1 <= k <= 10000. The entries of queries may be arbitrary 64-bit integers. All indices are 0-based.

statement: Whenever max_points returns a result ans, for every i with 0 <= i < k, if queries[i] > grid[r][c] for all r,c with 0 <= r < m and 0 <= c < n, then ans[i] = m*n.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). We assume m >= 1; n >= 1; every row grid[r] with 0 <= r < m has length exactly n; m*n <= 100000; for every r,c with 0 <= r < m and 0 <= c < n, 1 <= grid[r][c] <= 1000000; and k = len(queries) satisfies 1 <= k <= 10000. statement: Whenever max_points returns a result ans, for all i,j with 0 <= i < k and 0 <= j < k, if queries[i] <= queries[j], then ans[i] <= ans[j].
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). statement: Whenever max_points returns a result ans, for all i,j with 0 <= i < k and 0 <= j < k, if for every r,c with 0 <= r < m and 0 <= c < n the condition grid[r][c] < queries[i] holds exactly when grid[r][c] < queries[j] holds, then ans[i] = ans[j].
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). We assume m >= 1; n >= 1; every row grid[r] with 0 <= r < m has length exactly n; m*n <= 100000; for every r,c with 0 <= r < m and 0 <= c < n, 1 <= grid[r][c] <= 1000000; and k = len(queries) satisfies 1 <= k <= 10000. statement: Whenever max_points returns a result ans, for every i with 0 <= i < k and ans[i] > 0, there exists a finite sequence of cells (r_0,c_0), ..., (r_t,c_t) such that (r_0,c_0) = (0,0), consecutive cells are adjacent in one of the four directions, grid[r_s][c_s] < queries[i] for every s with 0 <= s <= t, and the number of distinct cells among (r_0,c_0), ..., (r_t,c_t) is exactly ans[i].
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). We assume m >= 1; n >= 1; every row grid[r] with 0 <= r < m has length exactly n; m*n <= 100000; for every r,c with 0 <= r < m and 0 <= c < n, 1 <= grid[r][c] <= 1000000; and k = len(queries) satisfies 1 <= k <= 10000. The entries of queries may be arbitrary 64-bit integers. All indices are 0-based.

statement: Whenever max_points returns a result ans, for every i with 0 <= i < k and every finite sequence of cells (r_0,c_0), ..., (r_t,c_t) with (r_0,c_0) = (0,0), consecutive cells adjacent in one of the four directions, and grid[r_s][c_s] < queries[i] for every s with 0 <= s <= t, the number of distinct cells among the sequence is at most ans[i].
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). We assume m >= 1; n >= 1; every row grid[r] with 0 <= r < m has length exactly n; m*n <= 100000; for every r,c with 0 <= r < m and 0 <= c < n, 1 <= grid[r][c] <= 1000000; and k = len(queries) satisfies 1 <= k <= 10000. statement: Whenever max_points returns a result ans, for every i with 0 <= i < k, if queries[i] > grid[0][0] and grid[r][c] >= queries[i] for every cell (r,c) other than (0,0), then ans[i] = 1.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). We assume m >= 1; n >= 1; every row grid[r] with 0 <= r < m has length exactly n; m*n <= 100000; for every r,c with 0 <= r < m and 0 <= c < n, 1 <= grid[r][c] <= 1000000; and k = len(queries) satisfies 1 <= k <= 10000. statement: Whenever max_points returns a result ans, for every i with 0 <= i < k, ans[i] = 0 if queries[i] <= v, and ans[i] = m*n if queries[i] > v.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). We assume m >= 1; n >= 1; every row grid[r] with 0 <= r < m has length exactly n; m*n <= 100000; for every r,c with 0 <= r < m and 0 <= c < n, 1 <= grid[r][c] <= 1000000; and k = len(queries) satisfies 1 <= k <= 10000. The entries of queries may be arbitrary 64-bit integers. All indices are 0-based. Additionally there is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 1000000 such that grid[r][c] = v for every r,c with 0 <= r < m and 0 <= c < n.
